newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares on rise despite featurless trade.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares on rise despite featurless trade.

text.p: Most Egyptian share prices rose on Sunday despite a below-average volume, the Capital Market Authority's report showed.

The CMA all-share index added 4.56 points to close at 371.16 points on turnover worth 81.4 million pounds ($24.00 million). Canal Shipping Agencies accounted for 36.37 million pounds of the total volume.
"No one is interested in this company, and we even exclude dealings on the share from the overall volume," Mohammad Abdullah, Intercapital managing director, told Reuters.
"Today was a regular, normal day, except for Medinet Nasr," Abdullah said.
Medinet Nasr Housing and Development was the most active share, with shares worth 6.58 million pounds changing hands. The stock ended 24 pounds up at 504.

"Medinet Nasr pulled most of the attention for two reasons -- first, it is confirmed that the firm has bought Nasr Utilities and secondly, a published announcement said that it would distribute free shares from next Sunday," said Abdullah.
"People who still own shares by the end of this trading week will be entitled to receive free shares," he added.
The state offered Nasr Public Utilities and Installation for sale through sealed bids.
The closing price of two millers and a bank rose by the maximum five percent by the end of trading on Sunday. Egyptian American Bank (EAB) rose 6.51 pounds to close at 136.87.
Central and West Delta Flour Mills went up 4.26 pounds to 89.54 while Upper Egypt Flour Mills closed 4.13 pounds higher at 86.81.
"Upper Egypt, West and Central and the Egyptian American Bank were the most attractive today, Youssef Khalil of Delta-EAB told Reuters. "There is only demand and no supply."
The index for openly traded firms rose to 529.86 points from 519.51 points and the rarely-traded "closed" firms also rose to 268.68 from 266.42.
Out of the 72 shares traded, 38 ended up, 20 fell and 14 were unchanged
